title: PR & Crisis Management
completion_message: ¡Impresionante! Dominar el vocabulario de Relaciones Públicas y Manejo de Crisis es una habilidad de alto nivel ejecutivo. Términos como 'damage control', 'scapegoat' y 'PR stunt' son esenciales para proteger la reputación de cualquier organización.

stages.title: Relaciones Públicas y Manejo de Crisis (C1)

parts.visual:
Vocabulario de Crisis: 
- Damage control (Control de daños / Acciones para limitar el impacto negativo de un escándalo). 
Ej: The company went into full damage control mode after the scandal. 
- Backlash (Reacción violenta/Rechazo público / Fuerte reacción negativa del público). 
Ej: The CEO faced a massive backlash after his offensive tweet. 
- Scapegoat (Chivo expiatorio / Persona o grupo que carga con la culpa de otros). 
Ej: The manager became the scapegoat for the company's failure.
parts.audio: Crisis Vocabulary. 'Damage control' refers to action taken to limit the negative effects of an accident or error. For example: The company went into full damage control mode after the scandal. 'Backlash' is a strong negative public reaction to something. For example: The CEO faced a massive backlash after his offensive tweet. A 'Scapegoat' is a person who is blamed for the wrongdoings, mistakes, or faults of others. For example: The manager became the scapegoat for the company's failure.

parts.visual:
Estrategias de PR: 
- PR stunt (Acción de relaciones públicas / Evento o acción diseñada para atraer la atención de los medios). 
Ej: That celebrity apology was clearly just a PR stunt. 
- Whistleblower (Delator / Informante / Persona que expone información ilegal dentro de una organización). 
Ej: A whistleblower leaked the documents to the press. 
- Spin (Sesgar la información / Presentar la información de forma favorable para la empresa). 
Ej: The spokesperson tried to put a positive spin on the layoffs.
parts.audio: P R Strategies. A 'P R stunt' is a planned event or action designed to attract media attention. For example: That celebrity apology was clearly just a P R stunt. A 'Whistleblower' is a person who informs on a person or organization engaged in an illicit activity. For example: A whistleblower leaked the documents to the press. 'Spin' means to present information in a biased or favorable way. For example: The spokesperson tried to put a positive spin on the layoffs.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de PR o manejo de crisis correcto.

questions.question: After the oil spill, the company launched a massive ____ campaign to fix their image. (Control de daños).
The new policy caused a huge public ____, with thousands of angry tweets. (Reacción negativa masiva).
questions.explanation: Backlash = rechazo/reacción negativa fuerte del público.

questions.question: Instead of firing the whole board, they made one junior employee the ____ for the accounting fraud. (Chivo expiatorio).
Critics said the CEO's public apology on television was just a ____ stunt. (Estrategia de relaciones públicas).
questions.explanation: PR stunt = acción diseñada para generar cobertura mediática.

questions.question: The ____ who leaked internal financial documents saved the company from further fraud. (Informante / Delator).
questions.explanation: Whistleblower = informante, delator (generalmente por una causa justa).

questions.question: The communications team tried to ____ the news to make the layoffs sound positive. (Sesgar la información favorablemente).
questions.explanation: Spin = sesgar/presentar la información de manera favorable.

questions.question: We need to ____ a press conference immediately to address the rumors. (Convocar).
questions.explanation: Call a press conference = convocar una conferencia de prensa.

questions.question: A statement issued to newspapers and broadcasters about a newsworthy event is called a press ____. (Comunicado de prensa).
The company tried to ____ the scandal by releasing good news the same day. (Enterrar/Eclipsar).
questions.explanation: To bury bad news = enterrar malas noticias lanzando otras más positivas al mismo tiempo.

questions.question: After the scandal, their brand ____ took a huge hit. (Reputación de marca).
The CEO was asked to step down due to concerns about ____ of interest. (Conflicto de intereses).
questions.explanation: Conflict of interest = conflicto de intereses.

questions.question: After the CEO resigned, the board launched an internal ____ to find out what happened. (Investigación).
questions.explanation: Internal inquiry = investigación interna. (inquiry/investigation son intercambiables en este contexto).

questions.question: The company issued a public ____ for the harm caused by their faulty product. (Disculpa pública).
When a product has a flaw and the company asks customers to return it, this is called a product ____. (Retiro / Llamado a revisión).
questions.explanation: Product recall = retiro de un producto del mercado por defectos o peligros.

questions.question: The scandal created a massive ____ risk for the company's investors. (Riesgo de reputación).
The company hired a ____ firm to improve its public image after the scandal. (Empresa de relaciones públicas).
questions.explanation: PR firm = empresa de Relaciones Públicas.

questions.question: The celebrity tried to ____ the narrative by giving exclusive interviews. (Controlar).
questions.explanation: Control the narrative = controlar el relato/la narrativa.

questions.question: In a press conference, the spokesperson said 'No ____.' (Sin comentarios).
questions.explanation: No comment = sin comentarios (frase estándar para evitar declaraciones).

questions.question: The social media ____ from angry customers was overwhelming after the CEO's speech. (Repercusión / Reacción en cadena).
questions.explanation: Fallout = consecuencias negativas, repercusiones de una situación.

questions.question: The charity work they did was seen by many as a ____, not genuine philanthropy. (Estratagema de imagen).
questions.explanation: PR stunt = acción de imagen calculada para mejorar la percepción pública.
